The fix's new sentence claims to be 'a plain-English restatement of the reference parser's regex below, nothing more' and lists 'a trailing `**`/`__` closing the emphasis, a space, an em dash, a paren, or end-of-line' as boundaries. docs-writer tested each case in python3 against ^(Done|...)\b after stripping leading emphasis and reported the output: `Done**` True, `Done ` True, `Done—x` True, `Done(x)` True, `Done` True, `Donex` False, `Done_x` FALSE. Underscore is a \w character, so a TRAILING `__` is not a word boundary and `__Done__` would fail to match after its leading `__` is stripped - exactly half of the '`**`/`__`' clause is false about the regex it claims to restate 'nothing more'. The orchestrator ran an independent boundary replay at Gate 1 covering closing emphasis, space, em dash, paren, EOL, fused word, hyphen, comma and colon, and found the enumerated cases all behave as claimed but that the sentence's closing clause 'anything else ... does not match' is over-broad in the other direction, since hyphen, comma and colon also match; the orchestrator did not test the `__` case, so docs-writer's finding is its own. NO COUNTING DIFFERENCE TODAY: docs-writer independently recounted all 126 Index rows, all parse, 86 Done / 40 other, matching the rollup - no row uses `__`. Proposed replacement: name `**` as the boundary and state that a trailing `__` does NOT close it, directing editors to use `**` in Status cells.
classification: wording: a stated restatement of a regex that misdescribes one of the cases it enumerates
